cases.about: русский, слабый: общие слова, нет своего примера
cases.draft:
Я хочу поступить в AUCA, потому что это очень хороший университет. Там учатся студенты из разных стран и преподают на английском языке. Я всегда любил учиться и хочу получить хорошее образование. Моя мечта — стать успешным человеком и помогать своей семье и своей стране.

Я думаю, что учёба в AUCA поможет мне достичь моих целей. После учёбы я хочу работать в большой компании и потом открыть свой бизнес.

Больше всего я увлекаюсь компьютерами. Я часто сижу за компьютером, и мне нравится разбираться, как всё работает. Это повлияло на мою жизнь, потому что я решил выбрать специальность Software Engineering.

Я ответственный, трудолюбивый и целеустремлённый. Я уверен, что буду хорошим студентом и не подведу университет. Спасибо за внимание.

cases.about: английский, приличный: есть случай из жизни, слабая связь с программой
cases.draft:
Every Thursday my mother takes a bag of dried apricots from our garden in Istaravshan to the bazaar. For years she sold them to one trader at whatever price he named. Last spring I asked her why she never sold to the buyers who came from Dushanbe. She said she did not know what they paid, and she was afraid to lose the trader.

That answer stayed with me. I started writing down prices at three stalls every week in a school notebook. After two months I could show her that the Dushanbe buyers paid more in May and less in August. She tried selling half of the harvest to them, and our family earned enough to repair the roof before winter.

This small notebook is the reason I am applying to the Economics program at AUCA. I want to understand why markets in small towns work the way they do, and why people like my mother lose money because they do not have information. I know my notebook is not real research. I want to learn the methods that turn notes like mine into evidence.

AUCA attracts me because students from Kyrgyzstan, Kazakhstan, Afghanistan and Tajikistan study together, and many of our towns have the same bazaars and the same problems. I also want to study in English, because most of the economics I read online is in English.

After my studies I want to return to Sughd and work with farmers' groups, helping them see prices before they sell. What I feel most enthusiastic about is this moment when a number on paper changes a decision at home. It has already changed how my family plans its year.

cases.about: английский, далеко за лимитом 700 слов: отзыв обязан сказать про объём
cases.draft:
My name does not matter much for this story, but my village does. I grew up in a small village in the Rasht valley, where the road closes for several days every winter and the electricity goes off almost every evening. When I was eleven, my older brother brought home an old laptop that a teacher had given him before moving to Russia. It had a broken battery and only worked when it was plugged in, which meant it only worked for a few hours a day. Still, it was the most interesting object I had ever seen. I spent those few hours trying to understand every program on it, even the ones I could not read because they were in English.

At first I only played the simple games that were already installed. Then I found a folder with lessons about spreadsheets. I did not know what a spreadsheet was, but I liked that I could type a number in one cell and watch another cell change. I started using it to count things in our house: how many kilograms of potatoes we had in the cellar, how much flour my mother used each week, how many days were left until the potatoes would run out. My mother laughed at me at first, but in the second winter she started asking me to check the numbers before she went to the market.

When I was fourteen, our school got internet for the first time. The connection was slow and our teacher only allowed us to use it for thirty minutes after classes. I used those thirty minutes to watch videos about programming. I wrote my first programs on paper at home, because the laptop was often without electricity, and then typed them during the short time at school. Most of them did not work. I learned more from the errors than from the videos, because each error forced me to read the message slowly and understand what the computer expected from me.

In grade nine I took part in the regional olympiad in informatics in Gharm. I did not win anything. I solved one problem out of five, and I understood that the students from the city had been preparing for years with teachers who knew the topics. On the way home in the shared taxi I felt angry and embarrassed. But I also made a plan. I found a list of olympiad topics online, divided it into weeks and started solving one problem every evening, even when I could not finish it. The next year I solved three problems and received a diploma of the third degree. It was not a big result, but it was the first time I saw that a plan could change something.

At the same time I started helping younger students in my school. Our informatics teacher was also our physics teacher and our geography teacher, and he did not have time to explain programming to everyone. I organized a small group of six students from grades six and seven. We met twice a week in the classroom with the only working computer. I explained loops and conditions with examples from their lives, like counting sheep or checking whether there is enough bread for dinner. Two of these students later went to the regional olympiad, and one of them did better than I did at his age.

These experiences are the reason I want to study Applied Mathematics and Informatics at AUCA. I want to understand the mathematics behind the programs I wrote, because now I can make something work but I cannot always explain why it works. I also want to learn how to build tools that are useful for places like my village, where internet is slow, electricity is unstable and people do not have expensive phones. I believe that software for such places needs a different approach, and I want to learn enough to design it.

I chose AUCA because it is close to home but gives an American style of education, where students can take courses from different fields. I want to take courses in economics and sociology as well, because I noticed that the problems in my village are not only technical. When the electricity goes off, it is also a question of money, of decisions and of how people trust each other. I hope that studying with students from many countries will show me how other communities solve similar problems.

After graduation I want to work for a few years in a technology company to gain experience, and then return to Tajikistan to start a project that teaches programming to students in mountain villages. I imagine a simple system that works offline, so that a student can learn on an old laptop without internet, just like I did, but with better materials and with a clear plan from the beginning.

What I feel most enthusiastic about is the moment when a problem that looked impossible suddenly becomes clear. I felt it when my first program printed the right answer, when my mother started trusting my numbers, and when the student from my group came back from the olympiad with a diploma. This feeling has influenced my life in a very direct way: it made me choose my future profession, it made me stay at school after classes for four years, and it made me want to give the same feeling to other students.

I understand that studying at AUCA will be difficult for me. My English is still developing, and I have never studied in a big city. But I have already learned how to study with very little, and I am ready to work hard with much more. I am sure that AUCA is the right place for me to grow, and I hope that I will have the chance to prove it.

cases.about: английский, короткий вопрос в 300 знаков: приличный
cases.draft: Why does the dough my grandmother bakes in a clay tandoor in Kulob rise faster in July than dough kept in a warm room in January, even when my thermometer shows the same temperature next to both bowls?

cases.about: русский, причина вопроса; по знакам укладывается, по байтам портала — нет (кириллица — 2 байта)
cases.draft:
Этот вопрос появился у меня прошлым летом, когда я помогал бабушке печь лепёшки. Она всегда говорит, что летом тесто «живое», а зимой «ленивое», хотя зимой мы ставим миску у печки. Я взял школьный термометр и начал записывать температуру рядом с миской и время, за которое тесто поднимается на два пальца. Оказалось, что при одинаковой температуре летом тесто поднималось почти в два раза быстрее.

Сначала я думал, что ошибся с термометром. Я проверил его в кипящей воде и в снегу, и он показывал правильно. Тогда я прочитал в учебнике биологии про дрожжи и понял, что на них может влиять не только температура, но и влажность воздуха и мука. Летом мы покупаем муку нового урожая, а зимой — старую.

Я пока не знаю ответа. Но этот случай показал мне, что даже в обычной кухне можно задать вопрос и проверить его самому. Мне нравится, что наука начинается не в лаборатории, а с того, что ты замечаешь странное и не проходишь мимо.

cases.about: английский, приличный: три занятия, мало чувств
cases.draft:
In high school I devoted myself to three activities: the physics club, the school newspaper and volunteering at the city library in Khujand.

In the physics club we built a small wind turbine from a bicycle wheel and plastic bottles. It produced enough power to charge a phone, and we showed it at the regional science fair. I was responsible for the measurements and spent many evenings recording voltage at different wind speeds.

For the school newspaper I wrote short articles about science in daily life, for example why the river is colder in summer than the air. Writing taught me to explain difficult ideas in simple words.

At the library I helped younger children choose books and taught two of them to use a computer catalog. Once a girl came back and said she had read every book about space that we had.

These activities taught me responsibility, teamwork and communication. They also showed me that I want to study engineering.

cases.about: русский, в черновике имя, почта, телефон и ник — отзыв не должен их повторять
cases.draft:
Меня зовут Фаррух Назаров, я учусь в лицее в Бохтаре. В одиннадцатом классе нашу команду отправили на республиканский конкурс проектов, и за две недели до конкурса двое участников поссорились из-за того, чья идея главная. Один перестал приходить на встречи.

Я предложил каждому за один вечер написать, что он хочет показать жюри, и потом мы вместе выбрали общее. Оказалось, что их идеи не спорят, а дополняют друг друга. Мы разделили презентацию на две части.

Я понял, что в споре люди часто защищают не идею, а себя. Если вы хотите узнать подробности, пишите мне: farrukh.nazarov2008@mail.ru, телефон +992 93 555 12 34, телеграм @farrukh_naz.

cases.about: английский, учебный план без лимита: приличный, мало про исследовательский интерес
cases.draft:
Educational background. I graduated from a public school in Dushanbe, where I studied mathematics, physics and English at an advanced level. In my last two years I took an online course in Python and completed a small project that predicts the water level of the Varzob river from rainfall data published by the local weather station.

Research interest. I am interested in how cities in Central Asia can use data to prepare for floods and mudflows. In spring, mudflows often close roads near my home, and I want to understand how sensors and simple models can warn people earlier.

Motivation for further study. NCKU is strong in engineering, and Taiwan has a lot of experience with typhoons and floods. I want to study civil or environmental engineering and learn how such systems are built and tested.

Plan. In the first year I will focus on mathematics, programming and Chinese language. In the second and third years I want to join a laboratory that works with hydrology. In the final year I hope to write a thesis connected to flood warning, and later bring this knowledge back to Tajikistan.
